platformRules._comment: Sections 3 + 5: Generates Assessment Signals and deterministic scoring that leads to platform selection

scoringRules._comment: Section 3 – Each rule generates an Assessment Signal with Response Evidence, Interpretation, Why It Matters, and Platform Impact

platformRules._comment_platform_eval: Section 4 – Platform Evaluation (Strengths / Weaknesses / Risks / Alternatives)

Salesforce: Leading CRM and case management capabilities
ServiceNow: Strong workflow automation and SLA enforcement
Incident, problem, and change management built-in
CustomBuild: Full control over architecture and features

ServiceNow: Steep learning curve for non-IT teams
MicrosoftPowerPlatform: Not suited for complex enterprise processes
CustomBuild: Higher governance and security review burden

platformRisks.Salesforce: Vendor lock-in and licensing cost escalation are primary risks. Data residency and privacy compliance require ongoing attention for citizen-facing deployments.
platformRisks.ServiceNow: Configuration complexity and change management overhead are key risks. Ensure ITSM processes are well-defined before implementation.
platformRisks.MicrosoftPowerPlatform: Platform governance and citizen developer sprawl are primary risks at scale. Establish a Centre of Excellence and ALM practices early.
platformRisks.CustomBuild: High delivery risk due to custom development complexity, timeline uncertainty, and long-term maintenance burden. Strong in-house capability or managed services required.

platformAlternatives.Salesforce: If Salesforce licensing cost is prohibitive, consider Microsoft Power Platform for simpler citizen-facing needs, or ServiceNow for case management with ITSM integration requirements.
platformAlternatives.ServiceNow: If ServiceNow scope is limited to non-IT workflows, consider Microsoft Power Platform for internal automation. For citizen services, evaluate Salesforce.
platformAlternatives.MicrosoftPowerPlatform: If requirements exceed Power Platform capabilities, evaluate Salesforce for customer-facing needs or ServiceNow for workflow-heavy enterprise processes.
platformAlternatives.CustomBuild: Before committing to custom build, re-evaluate Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Power Platform against requirements. Custom build should be the last resort.

institutional._comment: Section 5 – Institutional Knowledge Confidence (deterministic signal quality, completeness, and score separation)

explanations.low: Limited institutional knowledge coverage — few historical precedents or scoring signals. Architect review is recommended before proceeding.

platformGuidance._comment: Sections 4 + 8 – Provides deeper narrative for Platform Evaluation and Final Recommendation (readiness, risks, governance, alignment)

readinessSummary.lightweight: Salesforce can support lightweight citizen-facing use cases but is best leveraged for complex CRM and case management scenarios.
readinessSummary.default: Salesforce is well-suited for citizen-facing portals, CRM, and case management at enterprise scale.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Simpler implementations may underutilize platform capabilities.
timelineRisks.default: Enterprise CRM deployments require extensive data modelling and integration work.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Salesforce expertise may not be available in-house.
timelineRisks.default: Third-party integrations and data migration are common delivery risks.

Salesforce.estimatedTotalCostUSD: Contact vendor for BC Government pricing
Salesforce.costExplanation: Licensing cost not calculated per governance request. Finance team to assess total cost of ownership.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Low capability gap — basic Salesforce configuration skills are sufficient for simple use cases.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: Medium capability gap — Salesforce Architect and Developer expertise required for enterprise implementations.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Low governance risk — standard Salesforce cloud security and privacy controls apply.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: Medium governance risk — data residency, privacy, and vendor lock-in require ARB review.

Salesforce.strategicAlignment: Salesforce aligns with BC Government citizen service delivery and CRM strategies.

readinessSummary.lightweight: ServiceNow can be configured for lightweight ITSM needs but full value requires enterprise-scale deployment.
readinessSummary.default: ServiceNow is the BC Government ITSM standard and is well-suited for high-volume IT operations and service management.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Lightweight deployments may not justify enterprise licensing.
timelineRisks.default: Complex workflow configuration and SLA rule definition extend implementation timelines.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Existing ITSM processes must be mapped to ServiceNow workflows.
timelineRisks.default: Integration with existing IT infrastructure and directory services requires careful planning.

ServiceNow.estimatedTotalCostUSD: Covered under BC Government enterprise ITSM licensing
ServiceNow.costExplanation: BC Government holds enterprise ServiceNow licensing. Incremental cost is primarily implementation and configuration effort.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Low capability gap — ServiceNow expertise exists within BC Government ITSM teams.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: Low capability gap — BC Government has established ServiceNow capability and governance processes.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Low governance risk — ServiceNow is an approved BC Government platform with established security controls.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: Low governance risk — ServiceNow is the BC Government ITSM standard with proven compliance and security posture.

ServiceNow.strategicAlignment: ServiceNow is the BC Government ITSM standard platform, directly aligned with IT operations strategy.

readinessSummary.lightweight: Microsoft Power Platform is the optimal choice for lightweight, internal workflow automation under existing M365 licensing.
readinessSummary.default: Microsoft Power Platform is suitable for internal operational tools but requires governance guardrails for enterprise use.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Rapid delivery possible — governance and CoE practices should be established early.
timelineRisks.default: Larger Power Platform implementations require a Centre of Excellence and platform governance model.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Citizen developer sprawl is a risk without proper governance.
timelineRisks.default: Complex processes may hit platform limitations requiring custom connectors or premium licensing.

MicrosoftPowerPlatform.estimatedTotalCostUSD: Included in existing BC Government M365 licensing
MicrosoftPowerPlatform.costExplanation: Power Platform is available under existing BC Government M365 licensing. Premium connectors and additional capacity may require incremental spend.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Low capability gap — Power Platform skills are widely available across BC Government M365 users.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: Low capability gap — Power Platform developers and solution architects are available across BC Government.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Low governance risk — standard M365 security and compliance controls apply for internal use.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: Medium governance risk — enterprise Power Platform use requires governance framework, ALM practices, and data loss prevention policies.

MicrosoftPowerPlatform.strategicAlignment: Microsoft Power Platform aligns with BC Government M365 strategy and digital workplace transformation.

readinessSummary.lightweight: Custom build is rarely justified for lightweight needs. Evaluate COTS options before committing to custom development.
readinessSummary.default: Custom build is appropriate only when no commercial platform satisfies the unique requirements. Requires strong in-house or contracted development capability.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Custom development timelines typically exceed commercial platform deployments.
timelineRisks.default: Enterprise custom builds carry high schedule risk and require sustained team capacity.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Ongoing maintenance burden must be accounted for in long-term planning.
timelineRisks.default: Technology stack choices must align with BC Government standards and long-term support capability.

CustomBuild.estimatedTotalCostUSD: High — requires full business case with Finance
CustomBuild.costExplanation: Custom development costs not calculated. Finance and procurement teams must conduct full total cost of ownership analysis before approval.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Medium capability gap — development team must be sourced and a technology stack agreed upon.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: High capability gap — full software development team, DevOps, security, and architecture expertise required.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Medium governance risk — custom software requires security assessment, accessibility review, and procurement approval.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: High governance risk — custom builds require full ARB approval, security threat model, STRA, and PIA before proceeding.

CustomBuild.strategicAlignment: Custom build is a last resort — only proceed after demonstrating no COTS platform meets requirements.

recommendationBasis.lightweightOrSmallOrInternal: Microsoft Power Platform is recommended for this lightweight internal use case. It leverages existing M365 licensing, enables rapid delivery, and minimizes incremental cost.
recommendationBasis.complexWorkflow: ServiceNow or Salesforce is recommended for this complex workflow use case. Enterprise ITSM or CRM requirements are best served by established government-standard platforms.
recommendationBasis.fallback: Platform selection is driven by deterministic scoring of assessment responses against BC Government platform standards.

strategicConsiderations: Align platform selection with existing BC Government enterprise agreements to minimize licensing cost
Evaluate vendor lock-in risk and ensure platform supports BC Government data residency requirements
Consider long-term maintainability and availability of in-house or contracted platform expertise
Ensure selected platform supports BC Government accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA)
Review IM/IT security requirements and complete STRA and PIA as required

riskWarnings.lightweight: Lightweight implementations should establish governance guardrails early to prevent uncontrolled platform sprawl.
riskWarnings.default: Enterprise platform deployments require Architecture Review Board approval and a detailed implementation plan before proceeding.
shared: All platform deployments must comply with BC Government IM/IT security policies
Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) compliance is mandatory for citizen-facing services
Data classification and privacy impact assessment required before go-live

opportunityWindows: Leverage existing BC Government enterprise licensing agreements to reduce time-to-value
Align implementation with current ministry digital transformation priorities
Build reusable components and patterns that can be shared across ministries
Engage BC Government platform community of practice for lessons learned and shared assets

categoryMatch.Architectural capabilities: Both assessments share substantive architectural capability requirements including platform features, integration depth, and operational scale.
categoryMatch.Business alignment: Both assessments reflect directionally aligned business goals, drivers, and strategic priorities for the ministry.
categoryMatch.Operating model: Both assessments describe a similar operating model including shared-service considerations, staffing, and delivery structure.
categoryMatch.Workflow characteristics: Both assessments involve workflow-driven processes with comparable approval complexity, routing logic, and automation requirements.
categoryMatch.Integration patterns: Both assessments require integration with enterprise systems at similar breadth and technical depth.
categoryMatch.Security requirements: Both assessments share comparable security, audit, and data protection requirements.
categoryMatch.Governance requirements: Both assessments operate under similar governance frameworks, compliance obligations, and ARB expectations.
categoryMatch.Platform selection factors: Both assessments weighed platform selection factors such as vendor maturity, ecosystem support, and delivery risk in comparable ways.

categoryDifference.Architectural capabilities: Architectural capability requirements differ in meaningful ways that reduce direct applicability of the historical precedent.
categoryDifference.Business alignment: Business goals and strategic drivers differ between the two assessments, limiting direct precedent relevance.
categoryDifference.Operating model: The operating model and delivery structure differ between the two assessments.
categoryDifference.Workflow characteristics: Workflow complexity, approval patterns, and automation requirements differ between the two assessments.
categoryDifference.Integration patterns: Integration breadth and depth differ significantly between the two assessments.
categoryDifference.Security requirements: Security and compliance obligations differ in ways that affect platform fit.
categoryDifference.Governance requirements: Governance frameworks and compliance obligations differ between the assessments.
categoryDifference.Platform selection factors: Platform selection criteria and constraints differ between the two assessments.

categoryReduction.Architectural capabilities: Differences in architectural capability requirements reduced the similarity score for this category.
categoryReduction.Business alignment: Diverging business priorities and strategic context reduced the similarity contribution of this category.
categoryReduction.Operating model: Operating model differences reduced the similarity score for this category.
categoryReduction.Workflow characteristics: Differences in workflow complexity and process design reduced the similarity score.
categoryReduction.Integration patterns: Differences in integration scope and technical requirements reduced the similarity score.
categoryReduction.Security requirements: Different security and compliance obligations reduced the similarity score for this category.
categoryReduction.Governance requirements: Governance and compliance differences reduced the similarity score for this category.
categoryReduction.Platform selection factors: Differing platform selection constraints reduced the similarity score for this category.
